scope: Seven selected narrative dimensions from two recovered copies; not a line-by-line critical edition, independent corroboration or historical chronology.

verse.text: Verse narrative framed through Indra and Narada; Nala and Damayanti enter the central story.

prose.text: Prose narrative of King Sudarshana, Queen Sudasha and a merchant’s wife.

verse.text: A kite carries away a Brahmin woman’s ritual thread beside the water.

prose.text: A cat carries away one of a merchant wife’s ten manda into the royal household.

verse.text: The king obtains the queen’s brata thread and gives it to the woman.

prose.text: The king obtains one offering cake from the queen and gives it to the merchant’s wife.

verse.text: Ten manda with chhena and coconut filling are named in the opening offering passage.

prose.text: Ten filled manda are named; chhena appears, but the filling list is not specified in the same way.

verse.text: Roasted fish return to life; a meal offered by the Brahmin household becomes ash.

prose.text: Roasted fish return to life; food is repeatedly spoiled during the royal couple’s stay with a merchant household.

verse.text: Damayanti observes the brata again while living in Bhima’s household; reunion and restoration follow.

prose.text: The merchant’s wife helps Sudasha observe the vow again; restoration of the royal household follows.

verse.text: Magha appears in the opening observance scene; Jyeshtha appears in the renewal scene.

prose.text: Ashadha appears at the beginning; Margashira appears at the later observance.

supplemental_passages.title: Rice and filling in another textual witness
supplemental_passages.text: The saved Odia Lakshmi Purana transcription introduces Sudasa separately from Manabasa. It instructs soaking arua rice and pounding it into flour, then making ten manda with banana, coconut, chhena and other filling ingredients. The cooking method remains unspecified. This adds a textual preparation reference alongside the booklet’s chhena-and-coconut passage, without establishing which text is earlier.

supplemental_passages.title: Who receives this offering
supplemental_passages.text: The transcription tells the observer to eat the prasada and withhold it from others, explicitly including a married daughter. This restriction belongs to the Sudasa instructions in this witness. It is distinct from Lakshmi’s later demand for food sharing across caste boundaries in the story, and does not establish how households distribute offerings today.
